1. For the price it's excellent, due to the following.
2. Has very high quality wallpapers to use.

                 ↑
For this to be true, do the following:
Start up app → Click Settings (Top Right) → Select "Pause" for first three → "Keep Running" and "Stop" for last two → (Quality settings are up to you) → Click General (Top of Settings screen) → Have first two checked → Scroll down to video settings → Enable "Video Hardware Acceleration" → Click "Ok" once done.

Summary of what those things do: Makes it so everything is paused when you're using a program, whenever you're looking at the wallpaper if it's animated having audio from minimized program on won't pause it unless you have the program popped up on your screen. For the Quality I recommend using max for everything, unless your PC can't run it. It won't affect performance so it's worth having the maximized if possible. For the FPS I don't see a difference when using 25 or higher, but I still keep mine at 60. The options checked in the General section make it so your PC starts up the program in the background and applies the wallpaper whenever you turn your device on so you don't need manually open the app to set the wallpaper. For Video Hardware Acceleration I've heard it makes the program run better and is used a bunch. 

Side Note: To get wallpapers either go to Discover or Workshop and look around/use search for more specific wallpapers. Double click on the wallpaper or click subscribe to download it which applies it. If you want to change it go to Installed and click on the one you want, to apply it either close out of the program by clicking the x at the top right or just click "Ok".

( Using "Stop" for the 2nd and 3rd option in the performance section of settings makes it so the wallpaper isn't applied at all when in another program and so whenever you go back to see your wallpaper the app gets opened again so the wallpaper takes 0.5-2 seconds or so to show up. Basically everyone uses "Pause" for those still because the Wallpaper will always be there and you don't have to see wallpapers switch out of no where whenever you exit out of a program. )

Look, I didn't come to Steam for another game to ignore. I came for Wallpaper Engine – the absolute legend that turned my desktop into a living, breathing masterpiece and simultaneously destroyed my productivity in the most beautiful way possible. This isn't software. This is digital interior design for your soul, powered by the Steam Workshop community that somehow keeps getting more unhinged (in the best way) in 2026.
You start simple: "I'll just download a chill lo-fi girl." Three hours later you're running a 4K 144Hz cyberpunk cityscape with raining code, reactive audio that syncs to your music, and particle effects that make your friends ask if your PC is a spaceship. The Workshop is pure chaos and genius – everything from wholesome Studio Ghibli scenes that make you feel cozy, to hyper-detailed anime waifus (we've all been there), to meme compilations that update with current events faster than Twitter. Got a new GPU? Throw on that 8K ray-traced masterpiece and watch your temps rise while your serotonin does too.
Performance? Shockingly good. My old rig handles complex scenes like a champ, and the new features keep it fresh. Multi-monitor support? Chef's kiss. Dark mode integration that actually looks premium? Yes please. It's 2026 and people are still dropping god-tier animated wallpapers with AI-generated art mixed with classic 2D animation – the community is cooking harder than ever. Whether you want relaxing rain on a window, a dynamic space nebula, or something that reacts to your Spotify playlist, it's there. And if it's not? Someone probably uploaded it yesterday.
The funny side of the community never dies. You'll see masterpieces, then immediately scroll to "Shrek dancing on my second monitor while my boss is in the Zoom call." Soft-hearted truth: In a world of endless notifications and stress, Wallpaper Engine gives you a tiny portal of joy every time you glance at your screen. It lets you customize your digital space in ways that actually reflect your vibe – whether that's serene nature, high-octane cyberpunk, or pure meme degeneracy. It's comfort in pixel form.
To the devs and the incredible Workshop creators: Thank you. For keeping this alive and thriving years later, for the endless creativity, for the laughs, the vibes, and for making every PC feel personal. You didn't just make a wallpaper tool. You made millions of desktops into tiny art installations.
If you have even a decent GPU and a love for beautiful (or hilariously cursed) things, buy this immediately. Your lock screen will thank you. Your friends will be jealous. Your productivity... well, that's between you and the lo-fi beats.

At this point it feels less like a utility and more like a full-blown hobby.
